title: Jade Lizard Options Strategy Explained: No Upside Risk!
summary: Ross Young (repeat guest, no sales motive) pitches the tastytrade Jade Lizard and Big Lizard: a short put financed by a short call spread sized so net credit >= call-spread width, which really does eliminate upside risk at expiry. He credit-selects strikes (put ~$0.70, $1-wide call spread) on cheap high-IV ETFs like GDX/GDXJ, 45 DTE, 50% PT (25-30% for Big Lizard), 3x-credit stop. The 'no upside risk' claim is mechanically true, but the title buries the real exposure: a naked short put on gap-prone gold-miner ETFs, and his 'close to 90% win' is untracked, self-reported, and inflated by his own admission that he refuses to close losers and rolls them out indefinitely (one GDXJ position for 2+ years). Real structure, honest presenter, no track record; the rolling that supposedly produces the win rate is loss-deferral, not edge. Write-up: strategies/jade_lizard.md (conviction 2/5).
